evidence.excerpt:
Deep research agents augment large language
models with external tools to answer com-
plex, long-horizon questions through multi-
turn reasoning. Learning from prior experi-
ence is crucial for continual improvement, yet
existing methods either retrieve verbose task-
specific traces that burden decision-making,
or distill procedural skills that remain decou-
pled from downstream policy adaptation. We
propose APEX, a hierarchical experience uti-
lization framework that organizes interaction
history into instance-level trajectory memories
and category-level procedural skills, and cou-
ples them through a closed-loop architecture
of Executor, Distiller, and Planner. The three
modules are optimized via a three-stage al-
ternating GRPO training paradigm, enabling
reward-guided skill distillation rather than
fixed-prompt generation. At test time, distilled
skills serve as procedural priors

instance-level memories and category-level skills,
preserving concrete task-solving traces while ab-
stracting reusable procedural knowledge for plan-
ning. ❷ Experience-to-Action Agent Loop.Built

stracted into skills, and reused for strategic plan-
ning. This design aligns execution, abstraction,

Planner Training.In the third stage, the Ex-
ecutor and Distiller are frozen, and the Planner
is trained through a plan–execute–evaluate–replan
loop. Given query q, retrieved skill guidance
RS(q), and retrieved memoriesRM(q), the Plan-
ner first generates an initial plan:
p1 =π plan
ψ (q,RS(q),RM(q)).(12)
The frozen Executor executes p1 and produces
the first answer ˆy1. The Planner then observes
Trace(τ) and predicts a binary decisiond∈{0,1}
indicating whether re-planning is needed. If d= 1 ,
the Planner generates a revised planp2 and obtains
a second answer ˆy2. Ifd= 0 , we set ˆy2 = ˆy1. The
Planner reward is:
Rplan =α1Racc(ˆy2) +α 2Racc(ˆy1)
+α 3Rfmt +α 4Rdec, (13)
where α1, α2, α3, and α4 are hyperparameters.
The decision rewardRdec encourages the Planner
to stop when the first execution is correct and to
trigger re-planning when the initial execution fails.

to stop when the first execution is correct and to
trigger re-planning when the initial execution fails.

Training Settings:Our training framework is
built on veRL (Sheng et al., 2025) and follows a
three-stage alternating optimization paradigm. The
Executor employs Qwen2.5-VL-7B (Qwen Team,
2025) as its backbone and is trained on FVQA-
train (Wang et al., 2017). The Distiller, based
on Qwen3-8B (Yang et al., 2025), is subsequently
trained on FVQA-train to distill accumulated ex-
ecution memories into structured skill documents.
The Planner, also based on Qwen3-8B, is trained
in the final stage on a mixture of FVQA-train (with
images discarded) and MATPO (Mo et al., 2025).
The Executor is equipped with offline text-to-text
and offline image-to-image search tools. A Qwen3-
32B model serves as the LLM Judger for reward
computation. More details are provided in Ap-
pendix C.

We conduct three groups of ablation studies to eval-
uate each component in APEX.
❶ Experience Utilization.We remove different
experience sources during inference.w/o Mem.dis-
ables the retrieval of concrete execution memories,
w/o Skillremoves distilled procedural skills, and
w/o Bothremoves both. These variants reduce the
average accuracy by 1.8, 3.1, and 10.1 points, re-spectively. This suggests that category-level skills
provide general templates for similar tasks, while
instance-level memories offer concrete problem-
solving examples; their complementarity enables
more effective utilization of past experience.

evidence.excerpt:
While APEXachieves the best average perfor-
mance across seven benchmarks and demonstrates
strong generalization to out-of-domain settings, our
current framework is built upon small open-source
models. Although APEXenables a 7B model to
surpass closed-source systems, we have not ex-
plored how APEXscales when applied to more
powerful backbone models. Additionally, our three-
stage alternating GRPO training paradigm, despite
its effectiveness in stabilizing cross-module credit
assignment and producing consistently improving
rewards, requires sequential optimization of the Ex-
ecutor, Distiller, and Planner, which may not fully
exploit the synergies achievable through end-to-
end joint training. Finally, our skill-guided TTRL
mechanism currently operates online at test time
without ground-truth supervision, and while it al-
ready yields significant improvements through self-
improvement,

end joint training. Finally, our skill-guided TTRL

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline results are reported as benchmark accuracy against reference answers on seven external QA datasets, independent of the LLM-judge rewards used to optimize modules.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are measured as task accuracy against reference answers on seven standard QA benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Module policies are optimized via LLM-as-judge rewards covering accuracy, skill quality, reasoning coherence, evidence grounding, and procedural alignment.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics directly support claims of gains over competitive baselines across both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, and the ablations substantiate the value of both skills and test-time reinforcement learning.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is evaluated across seven multimodal and text-only research QA benchmarks against base LLMs, search agents, and established memory-augmented agents, complemented by thorough ablations and token-efficiency analyses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes rely on standardized benchmark ground-truth accuracy metrics on external evaluation datasets rather than the internal LLM judge scores.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline experimental outcomes are measured using objective task accuracy against reference benchmark answers across seven standard QA datasets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: During alternating training and test-time reinforcement learning, module policies are guided by LLM-as-a-judge rewards evaluating accuracy, skill quality, reasoning coherence, evidence grounding, and procedural alignment.

primary.limitations: The authors document key limitations including reliance on 7B/8B model backbones, lack of end-to-end training synergies due to alternating optimization, and running online test-time adaptation completely without ground-truth supervision.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the roles of Executor, Distiller, and Planner, the alternating three-stage GRPO training objectives, and online skill-guided test-time reinforcement learning with alignment regularization.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents an adequately scoped and well-documented architectural contribution with clear empirical verification across established standard benchmarks and comprehensive ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces APEX, a hierarchical procedural experience utilization framework for deep research question-answering agents that structures interaction histories into instance-level memories and category-level skills, trained via alternating multi-module GRPO and adapted via test-time reinforcement learning.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents an adequately scoped and well-documented architectural contribution with clear empirical verification across established standard benchmarks and comprehensive ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors document key limitations including reliance on 7B/8B model backbones, lack of end-to-end training synergies due to alternating optimization, and running online test-time adaptation completely without ground-truth supervision.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
